channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Deepfakes and AI Slop Are Supercharging Misleading Political Ads
item.description: In this depressing era of AI slop, psyops and deepfakes in politics, is it wrong to yearn for simpler times?
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: India’s Youth Are Angry. Its Billionaires Are at War
item.description: India’s rich are just as furious as its working class, but their anger flows in opposite directions. While the “cockroach” movement grew from college students demanding fair exams to schoolchildren protesting broken roads — all training their ire on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government — the corporate elite have turned their knives on each other.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: Amazon Charged the First Price
item.description: Vickrey auctions, a GoPro meme merger and Kalshi gamblers.
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.title: Banning Kids From Social Media Is Only Half a Solution
item.description: Australia’s world-leading efforts to keep youth off social media are a closely watched experiment that more than two dozen countries are now trying to imitate. But the early data suggests it’s not going very well.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: The Grand Canyon Floods Point to Our Bigger Water Crisis
item.description: The reason most lottery winners eventually go broke is that they aren’t prepared for the unexpected influx of wealth. They blow it on luxuries, bad investments and long-lost relatives. Dry places face a similar risk when they receive a sudden deluge of rainfall. If they’re not ready to capture and use it, then the water can do more harm than good.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: Trump’s Drug Plan Won’t Fix Americans’ Healthcare Sticker Shock
item.description: Any genuine efforts to lower high US prescription drug prices should be embraced. But President Donald Trump’s latest deal with drug manufacturers to lower those prices, announced Monday, falls far short of the “real relief” from ballooning healthcare costs he has promised.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Jarvis

item.title: Britain’s Political Violence Threatens Politicians and Democracy
item.description: Lawmakers returning to Parliament Tuesday after the long summer recess will notice a new portrait commemorating Ann Widdecombe, the former Conservative minister turned Reform UK spokesperson who was killed in July. And that won’t be the only reminder of that tragic event: Dozens of police and security staff will be arriving in Westminster, picking up passes and acquainting themselves with the lay of the land.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: AI Generated Campaign Ads Are Eroding Trust in US Elections
item.description: AI slop is taking over political communication. What could go wrong?
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Fed Rate: Warsh’s Pledge on Stable Prices Will Soon Be Tested
item.description: In his keenly anticipated speech at the recent Jackson Hole conference, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh struck a decidedly hawkish tone and assured investors he’s committed to getting inflation under control. At the same time, he failed to dispel uncertainty about his approach to setting the Fed’s policy rate. This puzzle will need to be resolved at the central bank’s next meeting.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Trump’s Job Approval Polls Have Reached a Critical Point
item.description: President Donald Trump can dismiss public opinion polls as “fake news” all he wants. That won’t change the fact that the commander-in-chief is in political distress — even according to survey outlets that usually give him more favorable ratings.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: US Venezuela Oil Deal Is Destined to Fail Without Democratic Legitimacy
item.description: Oil has what you might call a weak correlation with liberal democracy. Consumers have long tolerated being dependent on unstable or unsavory regimes for their energy. As Paolo Scaroni was fond of observing when he ran Italian oil major Eni SpA, no one drills for oil in Switzerland.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: Bessent Channels His Inner Spike Lee on Japan
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called on Japan to hike interest rates by invoking director Spike Lee’s most famous movie and saying that the Bank of Japan should “do the right thing.”
item.dc:creator: Gearoid Reidy and Daniel Moss

item.title: Labour Angst Over Migrants and Welfare Will Test Burnham’s Backbone
item.description: If there’s one thing Andy Burnham’s friends and enemies can agree on, it’s that the UK prime minister is “a nice guy.” Niceness is a bankable political asset. The PM’s allies point to an immediate “Burnham bounce” — his approval ratings are up in every demographic, except right-wing Reform UK voters. What’s more, his upbeat style has paid dividends in a three-point increase in GfK’s consumer confidence index this month, to its highest level since Labour took power two years ago.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens

item.title: AfD: German Far-Right Firewall Is Facing Historic Threat in Saxony-Anhalt Vote
item.description: “Let’s write history together” is a phrase one wouldn’t ordinarily associate with regional elections, which tend to be about local concerns rather than epochal change. Yet ahead of an upcoming state vote in Germany, the slogan has become ubiquitous at rallies of the buoyant far-right Alternative für Deutschland.
item.dc:creator: Katja Hoyer

item.title: Nepal-China: To Fix Flood Disasters, We Need More Giant Dams
item.description: In the popular imagination, there’s only one threat to picturesque mountain landscapes that can compete with the destruction wrought by flood disasters like the torrent that swept through valleys on the Nepalese-Chinese border: dams.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling
